resolutions.rationale: Linford's explicit three-case weighted-average analysis gives the uncertainty claim a concrete probability-theoretic warrant, although it does not establish that every defensible distribution is unavailable.

Donahue gives a recognizable equal-range assumption and connects divine goodness to conscious and aesthetic value, but neither the parameter measure nor the weighting of divine aims is adequately defended.

The source responsibly rejects the advertised extreme confirmation factor as assumption-dependent, but it supplies no calculation or independent warrant for the remaining claim of a very large advantage.
A weighted average over current and future physics is internally coherent and answers the stated uncertainty, while the unsupported direction and size of the result remain a material inferential gap.

Donahue calls the weighted quantity difficult to calculate and then offers the ten-thousand-to-one illustration without showing component likelihoods, weights, or any derivation in the recorded passage.
If the weighted average really preserves confirmation after successor-theory uncertainty, it bears directly and substantially on the affirmative's deliberately modest strong-evidence burden.
The passage clearly distinguishes current from future physics and states the proposed averaging operation, even though its numerical inputs and derivation are left unspecified.

Reducing the extreme advertised figure is a genuine concession, but confidently labeling an unexplained ten-thousand-to-one residual as very strong remains markedly disproportionate to the support offered.

Linford supplies a specific counterexample: a smaller-than-Hubble-volume universe could be more discoverable as a totality, directly showing that the proposed aim does not uniquely predict cosmic scale.

The anomalous-patch analogy explains why uniformity may look preferable to one arbitrary exception, but it does not logically establish parity between unlimited personal attributes and the full disjunction of limitations.
The evidential support is principally an intuition about uniform laws and one anomalous patch; no independent prior rule shows how an unlimited God compares with all finite alternatives together.
The move directly confronts the live objection that infinity is merely one point among indefinitely many finite values by denying a uniform prior over that possibility space.

Establishing a non-negligible intrinsic prior for the unlimited hypothesis materially supports the modest Bayesian case, although this analogy alone cannot establish the requested evidential strength.

Donahue reasonably contrasts the unlimited hypothesis with an arbitrary single limitation, but probable comparability with the entire quasitheistic disjunction goes beyond what the one-patch analogy supports.

The neighboring-region principle and sunrise example concretely show how ordinary induction can proceed without global uniformity, though the proposed decline of support across distance is not formalized.
Donahue coherently separates coherence from modesty, concedes maximal scope, and proposes a comparative balance, but gives no rule demonstrating that coherence actually outweighs immodesty.
The decisive claim that coherence contributes more prior probability than unlimited scope removes rests almost entirely on Donahue's asserted judgment, with no source-grounded weighting criterion.
Donahue explicitly grants both the full disjunction and maximal immodesty, then addresses Linford's exact objection by disputing the relative weight of coherence and scope.
Preserving a non-negligible theistic prior is materially relevant to the modest confirmation case, while the unquantified coherence judgment prevents this reply from completing that burden.
The audio clarification confirms that Donahue corrects 'modesty' to 'coherence,' making the intended comparison between coherence's benefit and immodesty's cost readily recoverable.
Donahue concedes Linford's disjunctive comparison and maximal-immodesty point, then limits his conclusion to non-negligible probability rather than claiming dominance over the alternatives.

An immaterial designer consistently avoids the proposed physical-brain regress, and the stated weakening of induction in radically remote cases supplies an intelligible limit on the embodiment inference.
The passage gives a plausible reason to weaken extrapolation from familiar embodied minds, but this chiefly establishes compatibility and supplies little positive evidence for an immaterial designer.
Donahue squarely answers both elements of the challenge: an embodied divine brain would reproduce the regress, while inference from all observed embodied minds weakens in the creator context.
Removing the physical-substrate regress protects a subsidiary part of the theistic explanation, but it does not itself show that an immaterial mind predicts the observed fine-tuning.
The source clearly distinguishes a humanoid embodied agent, an immaterial mind without physical parts, and the weakening of induction when extrapolating to a remote explanatory context.
Donahue candidly grants that every observed mind is embodied and that an embodied God would inherit the regress, but he discounts that adverse evidence rather quickly through remoteness alone.
The audio confirms three distinct coarse options, but the passage neither shows that the partition is complete nor supplies a principled measure supporting the proposed one-tenth share.
Calling one tenth a reasonable probability understates the admitted dependence on how divine possibilities are partitioned, especially when each coarse category contains many finer possibilities.

Linford's contrast between speculative additional physical structure and a categorically supernatural agent provides an intelligible comparative-prior inference, even though the penalty's magnitude remains unstated.

The claimed differential penalty rests on familiarity with physical ontology versus unfamiliarity with supernatural agency, an intuitive contrast not independently connected to a defensible prior measure.

The source succinctly identifies the proposed distinction: extra dimensions add unfamiliar physical structure, whereas the supernatural-agent hypothesis introduces a radically different category of entity.
Linford expressly concedes that extra dimensions are speculative and then isolates ontological category as an additional concern, rather than treating mere novelty as automatically disqualifying.

The general Bayesian point that rescue hypotheses matter only by their prior mass is sound, but the exchange never establishes that multiverse proposals occupied the asserted huge share of naturalistic probability.

Several unresolved parameters can create cumulative explanatory pressure, but the move does not derive how their epistemic difficulties combine or why one successor theory must independently fix every value.

Naming entropy, Q, the cosmological constant, and the Higgs quantity makes the demand concrete, yet no dependence structure or model-space probability supports the claimed very small joint likelihood.
The reply directly addresses naturalistic successor flexibility by specifying that a successful deeper theory must cover the whole fine-tuned parameter set rather than isolated examples.
A defended cumulative constraint would bear directly on the strong-evidence motion, but Donahue explicitly says the point was not developed and leaves its aggregation insufficiently established.
The all-parameters demand is understandable, but 'cobble together' provides no clear aggregation rule and leaves the relationship among parameter probabilities and dependencies underspecified.

Donahue appropriately disclaims strict multiplication and admits limited development, yet still concludes that the joint epistemic probability is very small without enough support for that confidence.
No separate affirmative debate-wide consequence remains: the likelihood comparison, future-physics dilution, and final cumulative-demand strengths and gaps are already represented in scored moves.
No separate skeptical debate-wide consequence remains: uncertainty over naturalistic likelihoods, weighted-average symmetry, and auxiliary-hypothesis limits are already represented in scored moves.
